title: एकादशाधिकद्विशततमोऽध्यायः
titleEn: Adhyaya 211 · Janaka and the sage Panchashikha

summary.en: Yudhishthira asks how Janaka, king of Mithila, reached liberation, and Bhishma tells how he heard the teaching of the sage Panchashikha, who had been taught by Kapila. The sage taught that there is no self in the manner men take it, and that all things are caused by name and form.
summary.kn: ಮಿಥಿಲೆಯ ರಾಜ ಜನಕ ಮೋಕ್ಷ ಹೇಗೆ ಪಡೆದನೆಂದು ಯುಧಿಷ್ಠಿರ ಕೇಳುತ್ತಾನೆ; ಕಪಿಲನಿಂದ ಕಲಿತ ಋಷಿ ಪಂಚಶಿಖನ ಬೋಧನೆಯನ್ನು ಜನಕ ಕೇಳಿದುದನ್ನು ಭೀಷ್ಮ ಹೇಳುತ್ತಾನೆ. ಮನುಷ್ಯರು ತಿಳಿಯುವ ರೀತಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಆತ್ಮವಿಲ್ಲ, ಎಲ್ಲವೂ ನಾಮ-ರೂಪದಿಂದ ಉಂಟಾಗಿವೆಯೆಂದು ಋಷಿ ಬೋಧಿಸಿದನು.
summary.hi: युधिष्ठिर पूछते हैं कि मिथिला के राजा जनक को मोक्ष कैसे मिला, और भीष्म बताते हैं कि उन्होंने कपिल से सीखे ऋषि पंचशिख का उपदेश सुना। ऋषि ने सिखाया कि लोग जैसा आत्मा मानते हैं वैसा नहीं है और सब कुछ नाम-रूप से उपजा है।
summary.te: మిథిలా రాజు జనకుడు మోక్షం ఎలా పొందాడని యుధిష్ఠిరుడు అడుగుతాడు; కపిలుని వద్ద నేర్చిన ఋషి పంచశిఖుని బోధనను జనకుడు విన్న తీరును భీష్ముడు చెబుతాడు. మనుషులు భావించే విధంగా ఆత్మ లేదని, అన్నీ నామరూపాల వల్ల కలిగాయని ఋషి బోధించాడు.
summary.ta: மிதிலை மன்னன் ஜனகன் எவ்வாறு விடுதலை பெற்றான் என்று யுதிஷ்டிரர் கேட்க, கபிலரிடம் கற்ற முனிவர் பஞ்சசிகரின் போதனையை அவன் கேட்டதைப் பீஷ்மர் கூறுகிறார். மக்கள் கருதும் முறையில் ஆன்மா இல்லை, எல்லாம் பெயர் உருவத்தால் ஆனவை என்று முனிவர் போதித்தார்.
summary.ml: മിഥിലയിലെ രാജാവായ ജനകൻ മോക്ഷം നേടിയതെങ്ങനെയെന്ന് യുധിഷ്ഠിരൻ ചോദിക്കുന്നു; കപിലനിൽനിന്ന് ഉപദേശം ലഭിച്ച പഞ്ചശിഖൻ മുനിയുടെ വാക്കുകൾ അദ്ദേഹം കേട്ടതെങ്ങനെയെന്ന് ഭീഷ്മർ പറയുന്നു. മനുഷ്യർ കരുതുന്ന രീതിയിൽ ആത്മാവ് എന്നൊന്നില്ലെന്നും, എല്ലാം നാമത്താലും രൂപത്താലും ഉണ്ടാകുന്നുവെന്നും മുനി പഠിപ്പിക്കുന്നു.

source: Mahabharata, Critical Edition (BORI, Pune) 12.211; e-text by M. Tokunaga and J. D. Smith, © BORI 1999, version of Wed Jun 16 2021

verses.text: युधिष्ठिर उवाच

meaning.en: Yudhishthira said:

verses.text:
केन वृत्तेन वृत्तज्ञो जनको मिथिलाधिपः ।
जगाम मोक्षं धर्मज्ञो भोगानुत्सृज्य मानुषान् ॥

meaning.en: By what conduct did Janaka, lord of Mithila, who knew conduct and dharma, give up human pleasures and reach liberation?

verses.text: भीष्म उवाच

meaning.en: Bhishma said:

verses.text:
अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम् ।
येन वृत्तेन वृत्तज्ञः स जगाम महत्सुखम् ॥

meaning.en: On this they also tell this ancient account, of the conduct by which that knower of conduct reached great happiness.

verses.text:
जनको जनदेवस्तु मिथिलायां जनाधिपः ।
और्ध्वदेहिकधर्माणामासीद्युक्तो विचिन्तने ॥

meaning.en: Janadeva Janaka, king of the people in Mithila, was engaged in pondering the duties that bear on the life beyond the body.

verses.text:
तस्य स्म शतमाचार्या वसन्ति सततं गृहे ।
दर्शयन्तः पृथग्धर्मान्नानापाषण्डवादिनः ॥

meaning.en: A hundred teachers lived always in his house, each expounding different duties, speakers of various heterodox schools.

verses.text:
स तेषां प्रेत्यभावे च प्रेत्यजातौ विनिश्चये ।
आगमस्थः स भूयिष्ठमात्मतत्त्वे न तुष्यति ॥

meaning.en: Among them, concerning existence after death and rebirth, he held to the scriptures, yet in the truth of the self he was mostly not satisfied.

verses.text:
तत्र पञ्चशिखो नाम कापिलेयो महामुनिः ।
परिधावन्महीं कृत्स्नां जगाम मिथिलामपि ॥

meaning.en: Then the great sage Panchashikha, son of Kapila's line, roaming the whole earth, came to Mithila too.

verses.text:
सर्वसंन्यासधर्माणां तत्त्वज्ञानविनिश्चये ।
सुपर्यवसितार्थश्च निर्द्वंद्वो नष्टसंशयः ॥

meaning.en: He had settled the truth of knowledge in the duties of complete renunciation, his purpose fully achieved, free of the pairs of opposites, his doubts gone.

verses.text:
ऋषीणामाहुरेकं यं कामादवसितं नृषु ।
शाश्वतं सुखमत्यन्तमन्विच्छन्स सुदुर्लभम् ॥

meaning.en: They speak of him as unique among sages, who, born among men from desire, sought eternal and utter happiness, very hard to find.

verses.text:
यमाहुः कपिलं सांख्याः परमर्षिं प्रजापतिम् ।
स मन्ये तेन रूपेण विस्मापयति हि स्वयम् ॥

meaning.en: Him whom the Sankhyas call Kapila, the supreme sage and Prajapati; I think that in that form he himself astonishes.

verses.text:
आसुरेः प्रथमं शिष्यं यमाहुश्चिरजीविनम् ।
पञ्चस्रोतसि यः सत्रमास्ते वर्षसहस्रिकम् ॥

meaning.en: They say Asuri was his first disciple, long-lived, who sat at a thousand-year sacrifice at Panchasrotas.

verses.text:
तं समासीनमागम्य मण्डलं कापिलं महत् ।
पुरुषावस्थमव्यक्तं परमार्थं निबोधयत् ॥

meaning.en: Coming to him as he sat, Kapila's great circle taught him the unmanifest supreme truth, the state of the spirit.

verses.text:
इष्टिसत्रेण संसिद्धो भूयश्च तपसा मुनिः ।
क्षेत्रक्षेत्रज्ञयोर्व्यक्तिं बुबुधे देवदर्शनः ॥

meaning.en: Perfected by sacrifice and again by austerity, the sage, who saw the gods, understood the manifestation of the field and the knower of the field.

verses.text:
यत्तदेकाक्षरं ब्रह्म नानारूपं प्रदृश्यते ।
आसुरिर्मण्डले तस्मिन्प्रतिपेदे तदव्ययम् ॥

meaning.en: That one-syllabled Brahman that is seen in many forms: Asuri in that circle attained it, the imperishable.

verses.text:
तस्य पञ्चशिखः शिष्यो मानुष्या पयसा भृतः ।
ब्राह्मणी कपिला नाम काचिदासीत्कुटुम्बिनी ॥

meaning.en: His disciple was Panchashikha, nourished on a human woman's milk; there was a Brahmin householder's wife named Kapila.

verses.text:
तस्याः पुत्रत्वमागम्य स्त्रियाः स पिबति स्तनौ ।
ततः स कापिलेयत्वं लेभे बुद्धिं च नैष्ठिकीम् ॥

meaning.en: Having become her son, he drank the woman's breast; from that he gained the name Kapileya and a final, settled understanding.

verses.text:
एतन्मे भगवानाह कापिलेयाय संभवम् ।
तस्य तत्कापिलेयत्वं सर्ववित्त्वमनुत्तमम् ॥

meaning.en: The lord told me this about the birth of Kapileya; his being Kapileya and his supreme omniscience are unsurpassed.

verses.text:
सामान्यं कपिलो ज्ञात्वा धर्मज्ञानामनुत्तमम् ।
उपेत्य शतमाचार्यान्मोहयामास हेतुभिः ॥

meaning.en: Knowing the general view, the best among those who know dharma, Kapila went among the hundred teachers and bewildered them with arguments.

verses.text:
जनकस्त्वभिसंरक्तः कापिलेयानुदर्शनात् ।
उत्सृज्य शतमाचार्यान्पृष्ठतोऽनुजगाम तम् ॥

meaning.en: Janaka, taken with love at seeing Kapileya, left the hundred teachers and followed behind him.

verses.text:
तस्मै परमकल्याय प्रणताय च धर्मतः ।
अब्रवीत्परमं मोक्षं यत्तत्सांख्यं विधीयते ॥

meaning.en: To him, who was very capable and bowed in accord with dharma, Panchashikha declared the highest liberation, that which Sankhya lays down.

verses.text:
जातिनिर्वेदमुक्त्वा हि कर्मनिर्वेदमब्रवीत् ।
कर्मनिर्वेदमुक्त्वा च सर्वनिर्वेदमब्रवीत् ॥

meaning.en: Having spoken of disgust with birth, he spoke of disgust with action; and having spoken of disgust with action, he spoke of disgust with everything.

verses.text:
यदर्थं कर्मसंसर्गः कर्मणां च फलोदयः ।
तदनाश्वासिकं मोघं विनाशि चलमध्रुवम् ॥

meaning.en: That for which one engages in action and by which the fruits of actions arise is unreliable, empty, perishable, fickle and unstable.

verses.text:
दृश्यमाने विनाशे च प्रत्यक्षे लोकसाक्षिके ।
आगमात्परमस्तीति ब्रुवन्नपि पराजितः ॥

meaning.en: When destruction is seen, plain before the world's eyes, even one who says there is something beyond, from scripture, is defeated.

verses.text:
अनात्मा ह्यात्मनो मृत्युः क्लेशो मृत्युर्जरामयः ।
आत्मानं मन्यते मोहात्तदसम्यक्परं मतम् ॥

meaning.en: For what is not the self, death of the self, suffering, old age and sickness: one deludedly takes it for the self; that is held to be wrong and other.

verses.text:
अथ चेदेवमप्यस्ति यल्लोके नोपपद्यते ।
अजरोऽयममृत्युश्च राजासौ मन्यते तथा ॥

meaning.en: And if it is so, since it is not found in the world, this king thinks it ageless and deathless.

verses.text:
अस्ति नास्तीति चाप्येतत्तस्मिन्नसति लक्षणे ।
किमधिष्ठाय तद्ब्रूयाल्लोकयात्राविनिश्चयम् ॥

meaning.en: 'It is' and 'it is not': when that has no mark, resting on what could one declare a settled course of worldly life?

verses.text:
प्रत्यक्षं ह्येतयोर्मूलं कृतान्तैतिह्ययोरपि ।
प्रत्यक्षो ह्यागमोऽभिन्नः कृतान्तो वा न किंचन ॥

meaning.en: Perception is the root of both of these, of the fixed conclusion and of tradition; for scripture, which is not distinct from perception, or a doctrine, is nothing.

verses.text:
यत्र तत्रानुमानेऽस्ति कृतं भावयतेऽपि वा ।
अन्यो जीवः शरीरस्य नास्तिकानां मते स्मृतः ॥

meaning.en: Wherever there is inference, or what is done and imagined, the deniers hold that the life is other than the body.

verses.text:
रेतो वटकणीकायां घृतपाकाधिवासनम् ।
जातिस्मृतिरयस्कान्तः सूर्यकान्तोऽम्बुभक्षणम् ॥

meaning.en: They offer examples: seed in the fig-bud, ghee set in cooking, memory of birth, the lodestone, the sun-crystal, drinking water.

verses.text:
प्रेत्य भूतात्ययश्चैव देवताभ्युपयाचनम् ।
मृते कर्मनिवृत्तिश्च प्रमाणमिति निश्चयः ॥

meaning.en: After death the passing of beings, prayer to the gods, and the cessation of action in the dead: this, they conclude, is proof.

verses.text:
न त्वेते हेतवः सन्ति ये केचिन्मूर्तिसंस्थिताः ।
अमर्त्यस्य हि मर्त्येन सामान्यं नोपपद्यते ॥

meaning.en: But none of these reasons that rest on a form holds; for no likeness can be made between the immortal and the mortal.

verses.text:
अविद्याकर्मचेष्टानां केचिदाहुः पुनर्भवम् ।
कारणं लोभमोहौ तु दोषाणां च निषेवणम् ॥

meaning.en: Some say rebirth comes from deeds driven by ignorance; the cause is greed and delusion and indulgence in faults.

verses.text:
अविद्यां क्षेत्रमाहुर्हि कर्म बीजं तथा कृतम् ।
तृष्णासंजननं स्नेह एष तेषां पुनर्भवः ॥

meaning.en: They call ignorance the field, action the seed sown, and attachment the producer of craving; that is their rebirth.

verses.text:
तस्मिन्व्यूढे च दग्धे च चित्ते मरणधर्मिणि ।
अन्योऽन्याज्जायते देहस्तमाहुः सत्त्वसंक्षयम् ॥

meaning.en: When that is set out and burnt, with the mind subject to death, another body is born from another; they call it the wasting of being.

verses.text:
यदा स रूपतश्चान्यो जातितः श्रुतितोऽर्थतः ।
कथमस्मिन्स इत्येव संबन्धः स्यादसंहितः ॥

meaning.en: If he is different in form, birth, learning and aim, how can the claim 'he is in this one' be a connection, since they are not joined?

verses.text:
एवं सति च का प्रीतिर्दानविद्यातपोबलैः ।
यदन्याचरितं कर्म सर्वमन्यः प्रपद्यते ॥

meaning.en: If so, what joy is there in gifts, learning, austerity or strength, if whatever deed one does, another reaps in full?

verses.text:
यदा ह्ययमिहैवान्यैः प्राकृतैर्दुःखितो भवेत् ।
सुखितैर्दुःखितैर्वापि दृश्योऽप्यस्य विनिर्णयः ॥

meaning.en: When a person here is made to suffer by other ordinary people, or by the happy or the unhappy, the outcome of it can be seen.

verses.text:
तथा हि मुसलैर्हन्युः शरीरं तत्पुनर्भवेत् ।
पृथग्ज्ञानं यदन्यच्च येनैतन्नोपलभ्यते ॥

meaning.en: So, if they beat the body with pestles, it would be reborn; there is a separate knowing, other than this, by which this is not perceived.

verses.text:
ऋतुः संवत्सरस्तिथ्यः शीतोष्णे च प्रियाप्रिये ।
यथातीतानि पश्यन्ति तादृशः सत्त्वसंक्षयः ॥

meaning.en: Season, year, lunar days, cold and heat, the pleasant and unpleasant: as these are seen to pass, so is the wasting of being.

verses.text:
जरया हि परीतस्य मृत्युना वा विनाशिना ।
दुर्बलं दुर्बलं पूर्वं गृहस्येव विनश्यति ॥

meaning.en: For one beset by old age or by destroying death, the weaker parts go first, like the weak parts of a house.

verses.text:
इन्द्रियाणि मनो वायुः शोणितं मांसमस्थि च ।
आनुपूर्व्या विनश्यन्ति स्वं धातुमुपयान्ति च ॥

meaning.en: The senses, mind, breath, blood, flesh and bone perish in order and return to their own element.

verses.text:
लोकयात्राविधानं च दानधर्मफलागमः ।
यदर्थं वेदशब्दाश्च व्यवहाराश्च लौकिकाः ॥

meaning.en: The ordering of worldly life, the fruit of gifts and dharma, and that for which the Vedic words and worldly dealings exist:

verses.text:
इति सम्यङ्मनस्येते बहवः सन्ति हेतवः ।
एतदस्तीदमस्तीति न किंचित्प्रतिपद्यते ॥

meaning.en: thus there are many reasons in the mind; but 'this is so, that is so', and nothing is truly grasped.

verses.text:
तेषां विमृशतामेवं तत्तत्समभिधावताम् ।
क्वचिन्निविशते बुद्धिस्तत्र जीर्यति वृक्षवत् ॥

meaning.en: While they weigh thus and rush to this and that, if the mind settles anywhere, it decays there like a tree.

verses.text:
एवमर्थैरनर्थैश्च दुःखिताः सर्वजन्तवः ।
आगमैरपकृष्यन्ते हस्तिपैर्हस्तिनो यथा ॥

meaning.en: So, tormented by things profitable and unprofitable, all creatures are dragged by scriptures as elephants by their drivers.

verses.text:
अर्थांस्तथात्यन्तसुखावहांश्च
लिप्सन्त एते बहवो विशुल्काः ।
महत्तरं दुःखमभिप्रपन्ना
हित्वामिषं मृत्युवशं प्रयान्ति ॥

meaning.en: Wanting things that bring great pleasure, many of these unpaid men fall into greater sorrow; giving up the lure, they go under the power of death.

verses.text:
विनाशिनो ह्यध्रुवजीवितस्य
किं बन्धुभिर्मित्रपरिग्रहैश्च ।
विहाय यो गच्छति सर्वमेव
क्षणेन गत्वा न निवर्तते च ॥

meaning.en: For a perishing person with an unstable life, what use are kin and the winning of friends? One who leaves everything and goes in a moment does not return.

verses.text:
भूव्योमतोयानलवायवो हि
सदा शरीरं परिपालयन्ति ।
इतीदमालक्ष्य कुतो रतिर्भवे-
द्विनाशिनो ह्यस्य न शर्म विद्यते ॥

meaning.en: Earth, sky, water, fire and wind always keep the body going; seeing this, how can there be delight in becoming? For this perishable thing has no peace.

verses.text:
इदमनुपधि वाक्यमच्छलं
परमनिरामयमात्मसाक्षिकम् ।
नरपतिरभिवीक्ष्य विस्मितः
पुनरनुयोक्तुमिदं प्रचक्रमे ॥

meaning.en: This word, free of attachment and of deceit, supremely free of illness and witnessed by the self: the king, astonished, having considered it, set out again to question him.
